14302.question_text: The density of a certain oil on frying becomes 0.4 kgm\(^{-3}\) with the volume of 20m\(^{3}\). what will be its initial volume when its initial density is 0.8 kgm\(^{-3}\) assuming no loss of oil due to spillage?

Density (D) = \(\frac{mass}{volume}\)

\(\therefore Mass = Density \times volume\)

= \(0.4 \times 20 = 8kg\)

The initial volume = \(\frac{Mass}{\text{Initial density}}\)

= \(\frac{8}{0.8} = 10m^{3}\)

14341.subject: Physics
14341.question_text: A galvanometer with full-scale deflection of 10 mA is to be converted to a voltmeter with full-scale deflection of 5v.  if a series resistance of 498Ω is used for the conversion, the resistance of the galvanometer is ?
14341.explanation:
r = resistance of the galvanometer

l = current through galvanometer = 1mA or 0.01A

V1 = p.d across the galvanometer = I X r = 0.01 X r

: V1 = 0.01r

V2 =  p.d across the  multiplier = 5 - 0.01r


R = resistance of the multiplier = 498Ω
 

where R = \(\frac{V}{I}\) --> 498 = \(\frac{5 - 0.01r}{0.01}\)

CROSS MULTIPLY --> 498 X 0.01 = 5 - 0.01r

0.01r = 5 - 4.98

∴ r = \(\frac{0.02}{0.01}\) = 2Ω

= distance moved in the direction of force (which is the weight) when the body is released But cos 60o = y/0.5

Metals P, Q
original length lP, lQ
Increase in length ΔlP, ΔlQ
Linear expansivities αP, αQ

But increase in length, Δl = αlΔθ
∴ΔlP = αPlPΔθ
ΔlQ = αQlQΔθ

∴ ΔlP = αPlPΔθ = 2 x 3 = 1
ΔlQ αQlQΔθ 3 4 2


∴ Ratio of increase in length of P to Q = 1:2

14510.subject: Physics
14510.question_text: THe velocity of sound in air at 16oC is 340ms-1. What will it be when the pressure is doubled and its temperature raised to 127ºC?
14510.explanation:
The velocity of sound in air, V∝\(\sqrt{T}\), where T is the absolute temperature
Thus V = K\(\sqrt{T}\) or K = \(\frac{\text{V}}{\sqrt{T}}\)
V is independent of pressure and density at a fixed temperature.
∴ \(\frac{V_1}{\sqrt{T_1}}\) = \(\frac{V_2}{\sqrt{T_2}}\)
T\(_1\) = 16 + 273 = 289K, V\(_1\) = 340ms\(^{-1}\)
T\(_2\) = 127 + 273 = 400K, V\(_2\) = ?

\(\frac{340}{\sqrt{289}}\) = \(\frac{V_2}{\sqrt{400}}\)

∴ V\(_2\) = \(\frac{340 \sqrt{400}}{\sqrt{289}}\) = 400m/s

41403.question_text: The radioisotope \( ^{235}_{92}U \) decays by emitting two alpha particles, three beta particles and a gamma ray. What is the mass and atomic number of the resulting element?

2 Alpha decay --> 2  X  He\(^{4}_{2}\) = Element\(^{8}_{4}\) 

 

- Beta particles are high energy electrons-  e\(^{0}_{-1}\)

3 Beta particles --> 3  X  e\(^{0}_{-1}\) = Element\(^{0}_{-3}\)

- Gamma rays are waves of electromagnetic energy, or photons.

the mass and atomic number of the resulting element = U\(^{235}_{92}\) - Elements( \(^{8}_{4}\) +  \(^{0}_{-3}\) )

--> Element\(^{227}_{91}\)
